messages.subject: model (sigma~sessioncov) produces consistant sigma estimates across sites
parts:
I am confused by my model output and want to insure it makes sense based on model covariates. Specifically, my sigma parameter is a session specific covariate where each site has a different value but the output sigma estimates are the same across all sites... and I feel that can't be right. Model specifics follow:


I am running a multi-session model. For simplicity, this example shows specifics for one site.


Capthist_Site1<- read.capthist("Site1_Capture.txt", "Site1_Trap_wcov.txt", detector = "multi", trapcovnames = 'Cover')


Note: "Cover" is a detector specific, user defined, covariate added in the read.capthist step (above)


Mask_Site1 <- make.mask(traps(Site1), buffer=400,spacing = 25, type='trapbuffer')


### load sessioncov file ###

session_cov<-read.csv("session_cov.csv")


final model in question (sessioncov highlighted):


secr.fit(capthist = Capthist_All_Sites, model = list(D ~ session, g0 ~ k + Cover, sigma ~ act), mask = Mask_All_Sites, detectfn = "EX", sessioncov = session_cov, trace = FALSE)


Note: "act" is a session specific, user defined, covariate where each site has a session specific value associated with "act"

My model takes ~5 hours to run but does complete with no errors or warnings. The output for predict() for 2 of my 13 sites follow. Notice, in yellow, my "act" is the same across the two sites and my sigma parameter, in orange, is also the same across sites.

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: model (sigma~sessioncov) produces consistant sigma estimates across sites
parts:
Paul

I think you're seeing the expected behaviour of predict(): unless you specify levels of 'act' in a dataframe provided by the newdata argument, the reported estimates are for a single, arbitrary level of 'act' (the first, from memory). For this you save the fitted model (e.g. fit1 <- secr.fit(...)) and then obtain the predictions (estimates) with e.g., predict(fit1, newdata = data.frame(act = c(...))). newdata should include values for any other predictors (k etc.)

Note also that covariate models are very slow to fit with secr.fit when there are many levels, so you might be better to bin these.

It also helps to state the version you are using (note new release last week).

Murray
